## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.93); key evidence e2, e3, e4, e5, e6.

Why: Extreme bright bundled tubulin at two doses plus 6/10 atlas neighbors as stabilizers warrants conclusion.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Live-cell SiR-tubulin imaging plus phospho-H3 mitotic index to confirm stabilized bundles and mitotic arrest, with washout to test reversibility.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Top MoA Microtubule stabilizers over runner-up Protein degradation (0.03) is well-supported: extreme tubulin gains at two independent doses (1 uM dose7 rep1: tub_glcm_contrast z=+108.2, tub_mean z=+25.1; 0.03 uM dose4 rep1: z=+62.9, +22.25) with thick bright bundles/rings on visual review at both doses, atlas 6/10 stabilizers with top similarities 0.90-0.924 vs 2/10 protein-degradation at lower similarity. This is opposite to destabilizer loss and not equally explained by Aurora or protein degradation. Two-dose consistency mitigates the single-replicate-per-dose concern; the effect is massive, not weak. Probability 0.93 is calibrated.

## Unblinding

Compound: **docetaxel** (PubChem CID [148124](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/148124))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: Tubulin inhibitor; Tubulin stabiliser

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Microtubule stabilizers**.

## Reflection

Acquiring the highest dose first (1 uM, w_df2909f8b4) was decisive: tub_glcm_contrast z=+108.2 with tub_std z=+32.4 and tub_mean z=+25.1 is the opposite of destabilizer loss and immediately favored bundling. Repeating at a 30-fold lower mid dose (0.03 uM, w_13ba1079c0) with the same direction (tub_glcm_contrast z=+62.9, tub_std z=+22.3) showed dose-persistence, and two independent visual checks both called Microtubule stabilizers with lower density vs DMSO.
Comparison to the reference atlas locked the call: 6/10 neighbors were Microtubule stabilizers versus only 2/10 Protein degradation and 1/10 Cholesterol-lowering, supporting Microtubule stabilizers at 0.93. Unblinding as docetaxel with ChEMBL Tubulin stabiliser agreed, consistent with taxane stabilization of microtubules (PMID 36876916) and taxane-microtubule action (PMID 18068131).
The main distraction was over-weighting minority atlas hits and the large nuclear shape change (nuc_form_factor z=-26.2) without explaining it as secondary mitotic distortion. I also left single-replicate-per-dose risk by using only 2 wells with no low-dose or DMSO control acquisition, and the second literature search on bundling phenotype returned 0 hits, adding nothing.

What was right:
- High-dose tubulin texture/intensity spike (tub_glcm_contrast z=+108.2, tub_mean z=+25.1) correctly flagged bright bundling rather than destabilizer loss
- Mid-dose replication at 0.03 uM (tub_glcm_contrast z=+62.9) showed same direction, establishing persistence across doses
- Visual phenotype of thick bright bundles/rings at both doses matched the quantitative tubulin gains
- Atlas match at 6/10 Microtubule stabilizers correctly outweighed 2/10 Protein degradation and 1/10 Cholesterol-lowering

What was wrong or missed:
- Retained Protein degradation at 0.03 and Microtubule destabilizers/Aurora at 0.02 despite quantitative and visual evidence contradicting them; minority atlas neighbors were over-weighted
- Noted nuc_form_factor z=-26.2 but did not mechanistically resolve whether it was secondary mitotic distortion versus direct nuclear effect
- Acquired only one replicate per dose with no DMSO or low-dose control, leaving single-replicate risk mitigated only by huge effect size
- Ran a second literature search that returned 0 hits and duplicated compound lookup without adding discrimination

Proposed next experiment: Live-cell SiR-tubulin time-lapse at 0.03 and 1 uM with washout plus phospho-H3 mitotic index and EB1 comet counts to confirm stabilized bundles, suppressed dynamics, and reversible mitotic arrest versus Aurora/Eg5 mimics.
